statement: Consider a limit with the certificate and local-kernel properties of Section 15, obtained with the moment compactness bound of Lemma 14.2. Either of the following assumptions is sufficient for exact-power upper endpoint moment control, compactness of the normalized backward quantum family (v ≤ 1) and each fixed finite forward enlargement, and a finite deterministic upper comparison with D. 1. For some K < ∞, qi ≤ K2−ip for every i ≥ 0. 2. There is an integer i0 ≥ 0 such that 0 < qi < ∞ for every i ≥ i0, and constants 0 < m < M < ∞ such that every own-unit law Gi, i ≥ i0, satisfies T (m, M) with probability at least 1 − ε0. Here ε0 > 0 is chosen sufficiently small, once, for the annulus-coverage threshold with favorable fraction 1/4 and this fixed geometry. The finitely many scales preceding i0 need only have finite endpoint norms and satisfy the given compactness bound. In the second case there is a deterministic T0 < ∞, depending only on m, M and the geometry, such that T−2 0 ≤ bi/bj ≤ T2 0 (i, j ≥ i0). (16.3) In either case, for a finite K′ and every i ≥ 0, ∥X2−i ∥k = qi ≤ K′ 2−ip . (16.4) Each fixed finite forward enlargement has the corresponding bounded-window controls in the retained base units. A change to its own units is allowed once its limiting internal endpoint norm is positive.
